questions.markdown: Write a recursive algorithm to solve the tower of Hanoi problem. Set up and solve recurrence relation using backward substitution method.
Write the pseudocode to find the GCD of two numbers using consecutive integer method. Compute the best case and worst-case time complexity of this algorithm.

For each of the following functions, indicate how much the function's value will change if its argument is increased fourfold.

i) $\log_2 n$    ii) $\sqrt{n}$    iii) $n$    iv) $n^2$    v) $n^3$    vi) $2^n$

Consider a simple text search feature in a word processing application using the brute force string matching algorithm. The user inputs a pattern to search for within a given text document. The text document contains 1000 characters, and the pattern to search for is abc. Calculate the total number of character comparisons needed by the brute force algorithm to search for the pattern within the text document. Analyze its time complexity also.

Consider a scenario where you have a knapsack with a capacity of 20 units and a list of items with their weights and values as follows:

| Item | Weight | Value |
|---|---:|---:|
| A | 5 | 10 |
| B | 10 | 15 |
| C | 8 | 12 |
| D | 3 | 7 |

Solve the above knapsack problem using the exhaustive search approach to find the optimal solution. Calculate the total number of combinations that need to be checked during this exhaustive search.
Sort an array of integers: $[8, 5, 2, 9, 3]$ in ascending order using the bubble sort algorithm. Determine the total number of comparisons and swaps required to sort the given array.
Enumerate the benefits of AVL trees over Binary search trees and demonstrate the construction of an AVL tree using the given list: 51, 26, 11, 6, 8, 4, 31, 21, 9, 16.
Illustrate the best-case, average-case, and worst-case scenarios (input case) in the quicksort algorithm, including an example for each.
Utilize a tree representation to depict the step-by-step process of heapsort for sorting the elements 2, 9, 7, 6, 5, 8.

Assuming that the set of possible list values is {m, n, o, p}, sort the following list in alphabetical order by the distribution-counting sorting algorithm: n, o, p, o, n, m, m, n. Analyse the time efficiency of this algorithm.

A hash table of length $m=11$ is to be constructed by closed hashing. Show the hash table after inserting the keys 30, 20, 56, 75, 31, 19 into the empty hash table using the function $h(K) = K \bmod 11$. What is the load factor? Find the average number of key comparisons in a successful search in this table.

Solve the all-pairs shortest-path problem for the digraph with the following weight matrix.

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
0 & 2 & \infty & 1 & 8 \\
6 & 0 & 3 & 2 & \infty \\
\infty & \infty & 0 & 4 & \infty \\
\infty & \infty & 2 & 0 & 3 \\
3 & \infty & \infty & \infty & 0
\end{bmatrix}
$$
